How to use these trade ideas

read this before using any list
Show the 6-step guide
  • 1. Check the regime gate first. When it reads OFF (Nifty 50 below its 200-day average, or fewer than half of stocks above theirs), every list is a watchlist only. In the 7-year backtest, skipping new longs while the gate was off lowered drawdowns by about a quarter and raised the edge per trade, but gave up some return (it sat out the 2020 rebound).
  • 2. Pick the list that matches your horizon. Top conviction: Stage 2 trend-template stocks ranked on relative strength, held for weeks to months. Opportunities: stocks that trip a rule (breakout, momentum, value, quality). Swing: RS leaders pulled back to their 20-day EMA, held up to 4 weeks; its edge in the backtest is small. Weekly: 2–8 weeks. Long term and Monthly: quality-first, 1–3 years.
  • 3. Read the plan columns. Entry is the last close; an order can only fill next session, so skip a name that opens far above it rather than chasing. Stop is 3×ATR below entry (2×ATR for swing). Target is 3R (2R for swing), where R is the distance to the stop.
  • 4. Size from the stop, not from conviction. Size is the share of capital that loses 1% of capital if the stop is hit, capped at 20% (marked *). A wide stop means a smaller position.
  • 5. Before acting, check what the screen cannot see: results dates, recent news, pledges and corporate actions, and the live quote and liquidity.
  • 6. Once in, place the stop straight away and do not lower it. If neither stop nor target hits within the plan window (20 sessions swing, 60 positional), review the trade.

How to read the track record

what each table measures and its limits
  • What is logged. Every daily refresh records Top conviction, Top swing, Top long term and the Opportunities list with each pick's entry, stop and target, plus whether the regime gate was on. Nothing is edited afterwards, so losing picks stay in the record.
  • Forward returns. The pick's return 1, 4 and 12 weeks later (5, 20 and 60 sessions), raw and minus the Nifty 50 over the same window. Win rate is the share that rose; Beat Nifty is the share that did better than the index. A pick counts only once its window has passed (Matured).
  • Trade-plan outcomes. Whichever the price touched first: stop (−1R), target (+2R or +3R), or neither by the end of the window (Expired, scored at that day's close). A day that touches both counts as a stop. Average R above zero means the plans made money at 1% risk per trade.
  • Regime gate and sector tables. These split the same picks by market condition and sector signal at the time of the pick, to show which rules earn their place. Picks logged before 31 Oct 2026 were backfilled as gate off: the Nifty was below its 200-day average on every one of those dates.
  • Read it with care. Entry is the close on the list's date, but a real order fills the next session, so results are a best case. Costs (about 0.22% a round trip for delivery) and slippage are not deducted. The same stock often appears on several days and lists, so the real sample is smaller than the row count. Judge it on many matured picks across both gate states, not on a few weeks.

Compare each list with Random picks on the same plan, not with the Nifty: the test universe is today's Nifty 500, the survivors, which lifts every strategy including random ones. The gap to Random is what the rules add. Swing trades last at most 20 sessions, so their per-trade numbers are smaller than positional ones by design.

What this test can and cannot tell you

read before drawing conclusions
  • Technical rules only. Fundamentals and valuation as they stood on each past date are not available, so conviction uses only its technical, momentum and risk parts. The Long term list (quality-first, on fundamentals) is not tested.
  • Survivorship. The universe is today's Nifty 500. Companies that fell out or delisted are missing, which flatters every strategy; that is why Random picks beat the Nifty here.
  • Execution. Entry is the next session's open and costs are deducted, but slippage, circuit limits and taxes are not modelled. Gap-downs through a stop exit at the open.
  • One path of history. The period includes one crash (2020), a long rally and a downturn. Results change with the period; treat differences of a fraction of a point as noise.
  • This is a personal hobby project for learning, not investment advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. The author is not a SEBI-registered investment adviser or research analyst. Ideas are mechanical screens on public data that can be late or wrong. Do your own research and consult a SEBI-registered adviser before investing.

Model POP is a distance-versus-IV estimate at the short strike; BE POP is measured at the breakeven. Model EV is the per-lot expected expiry P&L under the same flat-IV normal model: a check that the credit pays for the tail, not a forecast. Red EV means the credit does not cover the modelled risk. Max profit and loss are per-lot values from NSE chain prices.
